name: cmark-gfm
scope: Reference GFM/CommonMark implementation built from source by scripts/fuzz.py into .cache/tools/cmark-gfm-0.29.0.gfm.13/ (source tarball digest verified before build) and cached across runs. Used only as the `markdown`-target differential oracle (`cmark-gfm -e table -e strikethrough -e autolink -e tasklist -e tagfilter --unsafe`, comparing normalized HTML against Document::render_html(Dialect::Gfm, ...)). Never linked, vendored as source, or packaged into any crate; the pinned version matches the GFM example corpus already vendored at crates/core/tests/data/markdown/gfm-0.29.0.gfm.13.json.
backtick_cache_correction: scripts/fuzz.py builds an additional isolated executable from this same verified archive, preserving the furthest cached backtick closer in src/inlines.c (exact unique preimage and registered patch digest checked). Original binaries remain unchanged. Raw input containing a backtick selects the corrected independent oracle before execution; original and corrected output disagreements are retained explicitly. Both binaries and corrected source-file digests are recorded. GFM section 6.3 and actual original/corrected regression controls justify the one-site correction. Original source licenses and notices remain applicable; no source or executable is linked or packaged into production crates.
emphasis_floors_correction: scripts/fuzz.py builds an additional isolated executable combining the registered backtick correction with separate close-only/dual-purpose emphasis opener floors in src/inlines.c. Each exact unique patch preimage and registered digest is required. Raw input containing * or _ selects this corrected independent oracle before execution; original, backtick-only and combined disagreements remain distinct and preserve complete answers. GFM emphasis delimiter processing and upstream CommonMark cmark0.31.1 independently executed controls justify this correction. Runtime compatibility controls require all672 official outputs unchanged and record the ten unchanged reference/specification differences. Reports record archive, both patches, source and executable identities. Upstream licenses apply; nothing is linked or packaged into production crates.
destination_balance_correction: scripts/fuzz.py builds a separate isolated executable combining registered backtick and emphasis patches with one exact unique full-function preimage correction to manual_scan_link_url_2 in src/inlines.c: reject nonzero parenthesis depth when a bare destination ends. GFM link destination grammar requires balanced unescaped parentheses. Raw input containing ]: and ( selects this independently corrected scanner before execution unless an existing independently certified literal-prefix guard applies. Original and earlier corrected binaries remain unchanged. Full original, previous and corrected HTML outputs, separate counters, source/archive/patch/binary identities and actual primary grammar controls plus all672 official compatibility outputs are recorded. Upstream licenses apply; nothing is linked or packaged into production crates.
email_counter_correction: scripts/fuzz.py builds a separate isolated executable combining registered backtick/emphasis/destination patches with an exact unique extensions/autolink.c scanner-label preimage correction: reset np to zero for each retried email candidate. GFM extended email grammar requires a period in that particular address domain, not a previous failed candidate. Raw @ or & selects the corrected independent oracle before execution, covering entity-produced delimiters without output-dependent fallback. Original and earlier corrected binaries remain unchanged; reports retain archive/patch/both source files/all executable identities, full answers and separate counters. Actual primary controls include fully encoded delimiters, decoded escapes, valid final domain dots, literal code/HTML and explicit links; all672 official outputs must remain identical. This replaces earlier narrowly certified email HTML projections for new campaigns. Upstream licenses apply; nothing is linked or packaged into production crates.

name: llvm-coverage
scope: The `llvm-tools` rustup component's llvm-cov and llvm-profdata (installed alongside the pinned nightly toolchain: `rustup component add llvm-tools`) and rustc's own coverage runtime, used only for `scripts/fuzz.py`'s instrumented qualification binaries. No Cargo dependency or production instrumentation. Resolved via `rustc --print sysroot` so the tool's LLVM revision is always exactly the one `rustc` itself was built from, rather than a separately installed system package that could drift out of sync; `scripts/fuzz.py` still verifies both against this pin. The upstream license text is unchanged from llvmorg-22.1.8 (same digest, verified directly against the llvmorg-23.1.1 tag).
